label: rectifyesvalidation.vercel.app
title: EVM Resolve

Hidden input field contains a server URL and secret for Coinbase Wallet connection (https://www.walletlink.org/#/link?id=aca191c9768dfc0eace0b03dc861a094&secret=d14b2f03bee76a78f002f9da105461d0eb853465b9b494a2ffbd81bc0d407fd1&server=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.walletlink.org&v=3.7.2&chainId=1).
Page lists deceptive wallet rectification services (e.g., 'Assets Recovery', 'Presale Issues', 'Wallet Validation') to lure users into connecting their wallets.

label: defixs-finance.vercel.app
title: Defix-Finance | One-Stop DeFi Solution
reasons: Input field named `seedPhrase` visible in the page's own bundle — this is a wallet seed phrase harvester disguised as a recovery tool
Page copy promises to 'rectify all strange wallet issues', 'resolve missing or irregular balance issues', and offer 'ASSET RECOVERY' — all bait to convince visitors to surrender their seed phrase
Lists real wallet brands (Trust Wallet, WalletConnect, Coinbase Wallet) alongside the seed phrase input to establish false legitimacy

label: dy79f9ws2p-svg.github.io/claim-rewards-v1
title: Connect Wallet
reasons: The page has a hardcoded receiver address (0x7485f9633c1C8A33F758aA9533aC4A8cCef57038) and a function approveToken() that requests an unlimited token approval (ethers.MaxUint256) for that address from the visitor's connected wallet.

The page is designed to connect to the visitor's wallet and then present an 'Approve Token' button, which when clicked sends a transaction to approve the fixed receiver address to spend the visitor's tokens.
The page does not require a seed phrase but uses wallet connection and token approval to directly facilitate token theft from the visitor.
